title: Anthropic stock drops sharply after its blockbuster IPO
excerpt: Shares of the AI lab dropped sharply a day after its solid market debut. The AI trade continues to struggle, with Anthropic unable to revive sentiment.
content_html:
Anthropic's stock is back to earth with a bump, dropping close to its IPO price

By Pete Syme

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-20T15:25:30.864Z

Anthropic stock traded sharply lower the day after its blockbuster initial public offering.

The stock fell as much as 11% to $86, just above its $83 IPO price. The slide wiped more than $200 billion from Anthropic's valuation.

"While everyone focused on the price Anthropic managed to get for its stock, the bigger problem is becoming apparent," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG, an investing and trading platform.

"Insiders can sell 10% of their holdings from day one, a major wave of shares hitting the market, and from a company which is still losing money."

Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of $17 billion but a net loss of $23.3 billion. Still, investors are bullish about AI's revolutionary potential.

And as the first AI lab to go public, Anthropic is widely seen as a bellwether for the broader industry.

Anthropic went public at $83 a share — above its previously provided range of $70 to $78 — raising an initial $81 billion. That increased to around $93.5 billion after the IPO's underwriters exercised the option to buy more stock, a provision commonly known as a "greenshoe."

At Thursday's open, the stock soared 34% to $111.50 per share. That meant it debuted with a valuation around $2 trillion, temporarily making Anthropic the world's sixth-most valuable company.

Although the share price fell across Thursday afternoon, it still closed 17% higher on the day. With a valuation of $1.76 trillion on a fully diluted basis, it dropped below SpaceX to become the seventh-most valuable company.

Its market capitalization fell to $1.6 trillion, or roughly $1.15 trillion on an undiluted basis, on Friday.

Anthropic's IPO was hyped for months. It was then also landed with hopes of reviving the wider tech market after mounting concerns over the scale of AI investment and Nvidia's leadership crisis.

However, it looks like even a record-breaking IPO hasn't assuaged those jitters.
